title: The upgrade notice warns about a REVERT it has not measured, because it compares commits and reports bytes
body:
## Summary

`upgrade`'s pre-flight notice asks a question about COMMITS and then states a consequence about BYTES. When a source is behind in commit order but its vendored bytes are identical, the command warns

    this source is BEHIND what is vendored here -- upgrading will REVERT the runtime

and then, four lines later, in the same output, reports

    0 added, 0 updated, 31 unchanged, 0 removed, 0 skipped
    No vendored file differs; this tree simply now names where it came from.

**Both sentences are printed by one invocation and they contradict each other.** The alarm is loud, first, and false; the correction is calm, later, and true.

## Measured, not reasoned about

2026-09-02. Two checkouts of this repository, `49e8bb2` and its parent `08aa004`. `git diff --name-only 08aa004 49e8bb2 -- bin/devbin lib/` returns **zero paths** -- the two commits are a whiteboard fold and a docs deletion, so the seam is byte-identical across them.

A fixture estate installed from `49e8bb2`, then `upgrade --from` the `08aa004` checkout, produced exactly the transcript above.

`vendor` on the same pair is CORRECT and is not part of this issue: it prints `direction  forward -- the source is ahead of what was vendored` as one labelled field beside `31 tracked, 0 divergent`. It reports a fact about commits, labels it as one, and never claims a consequence for the runtime. **The difference is not the data -- both commands call `source_direction`. It is that one of them asserts an outcome it has not measured.**

## Why it matters more than a wrong word

The warning exists for a real defect (issue 0021): `upgrade` syncs unconditionally, so pointing `--from` at an older checkout silently reverts a runtime while printing `updated` per file and leaving `doctor` green. That is worth a loud line.

**A loud line that fires when nothing will change is how the loud line stops being read.** The `--from` argument is most often an older checkout for reasons that have nothing to do with the seam -- a peer's tree, a worktree, a clone made this morning -- and every one of those now gets a REVERT warning it should not get. The class this repository already named for the fleet applies unchanged here: *counting stamps counts re-vendor events, not divergence.* `seam_digest` carries that sentence in its own comment, and `upgrade`'s notice is the one place in the tree that still argues the other way.

## The tool already knows

Nothing has to be computed that is not computed today. `vendor_states` answers "would any vendored byte change" per file, and `upgrade` itself prints the true sentence at the end of the run. The defect is that the true sentence arrives **after** the reader has decided, and the false one arrives before.

## Fix direction (hv ruled: file and fix -- compare the seam digest)

Gate the CONSEQUENCE on bytes and keep the DIRECTION as the explanation:

- bytes differ, direction backward -- warn exactly as today; this is the 0021 case and it is real
- bytes identical, direction backward -- say so plainly: the source is behind, and no vendored file would change
- `unknown` stays `unknown` and must never be read as either

The acceptance test is that a source which changes no vendored byte cannot produce the word REVERT.
